text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 2 in history.
1492 - Spain re-capture the southern city of Granada from the Moors, consolidating the monarchy under Ferdinand of Aragon.
1727 - James Wolfe, British Army general, born. He led the army when the British captured French Canada in 1759.
1751 - Ferdinand I, born. Formerly Ferdinand IV of Naples, he became Ferdinand I, King of the Two Sicilies, when he returned to Naples (1816) after Napoleon was defeated.
1757 - Clive of India re-captured Calcutta after it had been seized by the Nawab of Bengal who had used the "Black Hole" to imprison British captives.
1788 - Georgia became the fourth U.S. state to be admitted to the Union.
1811 - U.S. Senator Thomas Pickering became the first senator to be censured when he revealed confidential documents communicated by the president of the United States.
1839 - French pioneering photographer Louis Daguerre took the first photograph of the moon.

1895 - Count Folke Bernadotte, Swedish diplomat, born. He was head of the Swedish Red Cross during World War Two and was shot (1948) in Palestine while working for the U.N. after proposing that Arab refugees be allowed to return to what had become Israel.
1896 - Starr Jameson surrendered and was captured by the Boers after his attempted raid on Johannesburg in the Boer War.

1905 - In the Russo-Japanese War, the Russians surrendered to the Japanese after the battle of Port Arthur. The Russians were trapped by the Japanese who had sunk merchant ships at the harbour entrance. The Japanese lost 58,000 men.
1905 - Sir Michael Tippett, English composer, born. His works include, the oratorio, "A Child of our Time", and the operas, "The Midsummer Marriage" and "King Priam".

1915 - In World War One, the Turks under Ahmet Pasha were heavily defeated by the Russians at the battle of Sarikamis. After five days fighting and a lengthy retreat, the Turks lost 77,000 out of 95,000 men.

1920 - Isaac Asimov, U.S. author born in the Soviet Union. A biochemist, he is best known for his science fiction writing. He also wrote informative scientific factual works, including "Inside the Atom" and "The Human Brain".
1942 - In World War Two, the Japanese captured the Philippines capital of Manila and nearby air base at Cavite.
1955 - In Panama, President Jose Antonio Remon was machine gunned while attending the Franco Race track in Panama City.
1959 - The first lunar space shot, the unmanned Luna I, was launched by the Soviet Union. It passed to within 4,600 miles of the moon before moving on to a solar orbit.
1971 - A barrier collapsed at Ibrox Park football ground at the end of the Rangers v Celtic soccer match in Glasgow, Scotland, killing 66 people.
1980 - Britain's first national steel strike since 1926 began. It was not settled until April 2.
1994 - More than 70 people were killed and at least 670 injured after two days of blistering factional battles in the Afghan capital Kabul.
1995 - The most distant galaxy yet discovered was found by scientists using the Keck telescope in Hawaii. It is estimated to be 15 billion light years away and was named 8C 1435+63.
1995 - Former Somali president Mohamed Siad Barre died in exile. He seized power in a 1969 coup and was toppled in January 1991 by forces loyal to faction leader Mohamed Farah Aideed.

1996 - Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak appointed Kamal Ganzouri, a deputy prime minister since 1987, to be his new prime minister after the resignation of Atef Sedki who had been. his prime minister of nine years.
